overall_reason: The article page has almost no motion of its own: the Industries and Technologies nav menus open and close in about 280 ms with a fade and a chevron turn, and the story cards declare a hover lift; the sweep raised no timing hits, but the declarations mix six unrelated curves, including ease-in on the nav toggles and an anticipating back-in curve on the button hover.

score.reason: T-PURPOSE, T-FREQUENCY and T-CHOREOGRAPHY pass (short menu feedback, no load reveal, no loops), while T-MOTION-SYSTEM finds six easings across 17 transitioning elements and ease-in or back-in curves on arrivals.

findings.title: The curve fits the direction and the scope
findings.where: nav toggles #w-dropdown-toggle-0 and #w-dropdown-toggle-1 (Industries, Technologies), the .button family ("Reach out", "Contact", "Discover GenAI Track") and the .story-card shadows, 1440
findings.evidence: dom-1440.json declares `transition: all 0.2s ease-in` on both nav toggles and `box-shadow 0.35s ease-in` on the three story cards, so their hover states arrive on an accelerating curve. The .button rule animates padding and background-position with cubic-bezier(0.6, -0.28, 0.735, 0.045), which the declared table flags as an anticipating curve (y -0.28).
findings.before: ease-in on hover arrivals; a back-in curve on button padding
findings.after: An ease-out (for example cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)) for every hover arrival, and no anticipation or padding change on buttons
findings.why: An arrival that starts slowly makes the nav and buttons answer late, and the back-in curve makes the button pull back before it changes.

findings.title: One curve family and one duration scale
findings.where: declared transitions across the nav, buttons, story cards and links, 1440
findings.evidence: The declared table lists six easings on 17 elements: the browser's ease (9), ease-in (6), cubic-bezier(0.713, 0.5, 0.165, 1) on the story-card lift (3), cubic-bezier(0.445, 0.05, 0.55, 0.95) on "Get in touch" and "Back to overview" (2), cubic-bezier(0.6, -0.28, 0.735, 0.045) (2) and cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.46, 0.45, 0.94) (2). Durations run 100, 150, 200, 350, 400 and 500 ms; the mega-menu links fade their background over 500 ms while the nav itself uses 200 ms.
findings.before: Six curves and six durations for hover colour, lift and menu changes
findings.after: One decelerating curve and a three-step scale (about 120, 200 and 320 ms) routed through tokens
findings.why: Each component carries the timing of the Webflow interaction it came from, so the same hover answer feels different on the nav, the buttons and the cards.

strengths: The article arrives with no load reveal and nothing moves on its own: no running animations, and the only infinite keyframe (spin, 0.8 s linear) is not running on the page.
The Industries and Technologies menus answer within about 280 ms (live run), close to the menu step, and the chevron turn shows which menu is open.
not_investigated: Passive motion: no passive recording, so motion that plays without a click is not verified.
Hover as it plays: the story-card lift, the .card-large scale(0.99) and the button background-position change are judged from declarations only.
The page's iframe: the capture did not exercise transitions inside it.
T-POSTER and T-DEMO-LOOP: no demo animation on the page.

Interruptibility and rapid toggles (T-RAPID-TOGGLE): no detector built. Gestures, scroll-driven and scroll-revealed motion (the capture does not scroll while recording) and route transitions were not captured.
The missing prefers-reduced-motion rule (A11-011) and the transition-all and layout-property hits (MOT-001) belong to the sweep.
